title: Polish a disk electrode in a figure-8, face flat
instruction: Polish the electrode's face on the alumina spot in figure-8 strokes, keeping the face flat on the pad with light pressure, then hang it in the stand's clamp with only its tip in the rinse water and let go.
context: Why: a glassy-carbon disk electrode is re-polished on alumina before most voltammetry runs, often daily, and robot chemistry platforms report this polishing as a manual step and a hurdle to automating electrochemistry. The maker's guide: keep the face parallel to the cloth, use a figure-8 while gently turning, about 3 mm of slurry, then suspend only the electrode surface in the rinse with a ring stand and clamp. The knack is contact control through a compliant arm: the face stays flat at light pressure while the hand sweeps two loops of opposite turn, and a tip held a few degrees off rides its edge and rounds the disk. Unlike grinding or filing down to a line, where firm pressure and the final shape count, here the load-cell force, the tilt and the path are what is scored. Then only the tip may go in the rinse: the shroud's upper part and stud stay dry. Done by: electrochemistry, battery and sensor researchers, lab technicians and students.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). (1) Load-cell platform: a 5 kg bar strain-gauge load cell under a 160 x 160 mm aluminium top, 4 cm tall, read at 80 Hz by an HX711 board logged to a laptop (about $20), centred at (25, 4); tared with the plate on it. (2) Taped to its top with double-sided tape: a 150 x 150 x 6 mm glass polishing plate covered by an adhesive-backed microcloth pad (Pine kit AKPOLISH); pad surface 4.7 cm above the table, wetted with DI water; a 3 mm round spot of 0.05 um alumina slurry (Pine kit) at the pad centre, (25, 4). (3) Rinse: a 100 mm wide, 50 mm tall borosilicate crystallizing dish with DI water 40 mm deep (water line 4.3 cm above the table), centred at (22, -16). (4) Ring stand: a 150 x 180 mm cast-iron base centred at (37.5, -16) and a 12 mm rod at (33, -16), with a spring-loaded burette clamp (e.g. United Scientific deluxe: rubber-sleeved, sprung jaws) on a 6 mm arm 6 cm up: its jaws sprung shut to a 14 mm gap (1,500 N/m each: about 0.75 N on the shroud; measure the real clamp's grip), the round sleeves flaring the top, 20 mm long and 6 mm tall, 4.7-5.3 cm above the table over the dish centre; the tip is lowered into them from above and hangs where it is left. (5) Lint-free wipe folded to 60 x 60 x 1 mm at (13, -5). (6) The electrode: Pine E5-series disk electrode tip, glassy carbon, PTFE shroud (AFE5T050GC): a 5 mm glassy-carbon disk in a 15 mm PTFE shroud 25.4 mm long, 49 mm overall; above the shroud the stainless threaded stem, about 10 mm across (estimate); about 25 g (estimate; weigh it). Thin painted rings on the shroud 3 mm and 10 mm above the face. It starts standing face-down on the wipe. (7) Gripper pads wear nitrile covers (cut glove fingertips). (8) Cameras: two close-up side cameras at pad height, one looking along x and one along y, each with a printed 3-degree guide behind the pad. Friction 0.15 on the tip and pad, 0.6 on the clamp's rubber (estimates). (9) REAL TRIALS use cheap stand-ins. Tip: an 18-8 stainless dowel pin, 5/8 x 2 in (15.9 x 50.8 mm, about 79 g; Zoro Select U51580.062.0200, $135.99 per 5), flat chamfered end down, rings painted 3 and 10 mm above that face, gripped and clamped on its side. Pad: a 150 x 150 mm piece of 40 um aluminium-oxide PSA lapping film (Nanolap 61606N, three 8.5 x 11 in sheets, $11.49) stuck to the glass, wetted with water, a 3 mm drop of alumina polishing suspension at its centre as the spot. PREP before each trial: rub the pin's face 10 strokes in one direction on 80-grit sandpaper so coarse parallel scratches cross the whole face; wipe it. Both arms start in their ready pose. One fixed layout, zero object jitter. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged from two side videos (scaled by a ruler on the pad), the load-cell log (synced by a tap on the pad at the start), a ruler and, in real trials, a photo of the face. FORCE: the load-cell reading. IN BAND: 1.0-5.0 N with only the face touching the pad, plate or platform (any other contact, e.g. a finger, the other gripper or the shroud's side, puts the frame out). FLAT: the shroud's axis 3 deg or less from vertical in both side views. TRACK: the face centre (the shroud silhouette's midpoint 5 mm above the face): x from the view along y, y from the view along x. LOBE: the track from one exit of the 10 mm radius circle round the spot to its next entry; it counts if it reaches 20 mm from the spot, its loop is 10 mm or more wide square to the line from the spot to its farthest point, 90% or more of its frames are in band and flat, none over 6 deg or 8 N, and no finger goes below the 10 mm ring. FIGURE-8S: the longest run of consecutive lobes alternating sides of the line through the spot square to the line to the farthest point of all lobes, and turning opposite ways seen from above, halved (10 lobes = 5, about 30 s). Gently turning the tip is allowed. POLISHED: after the trial, the face dried and photographed square-on from 10 cm, lit by one white LED lamp 30 cm away at 45 deg, a ruler in frame: the film's fine marks cross the coarse prep scratches with no patch over 3 mm wide showing only coarse scratches (a tilted face marks only a crescent). In simulation (no wear) it is met by the 5 figure-8s, whose lobes already require the face flat at 1-5 N. RINSED: after the last lobe, no pad contact after, the face 3-10 mm below the water line (between the rings) 2 s or more; the 10 mm ring under water at any time fails it for the run. HUNG: rinsed and held only by the clamp, face 3-10 mm under, both grippers 2 cm or more away, moving under 1 mm over the last 1 s. Ladder, first row that fits at the end: 1.0: 5+ figure-8s, POLISHED and HUNG; 0.75: 5+ figure-8s, POLISHED and rinsed; 0.5: 5+ figure-8s and POLISHED; 0.25: 2+ lobes; 0: anything else, incl. straight strokes and the untouched start. Sticky 0 even if put back: the tip drops (falls 20 mm or more held by nothing), or its face comes within 1.5 mm of the bench outside the wipe or of the dish floor. Possible: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Ends at the run limit or after 1.0 holds 1 s.
reset_notes: Pull the tip out of the clamp and wipe its face; re-dot 3 mm of alumina at the pad centre and re-wet the pad; top the dish to 40 mm with DI water; stand the tip face-down on a fresh folded wipe; tare the load cell. Real trials: photograph the face (POLISHED), then redo the PREP (10 one-way strokes on 80-grit, wipe) so the coarse scratches cross the whole face again; move the pad spot to a fresh area of the lapping film once the old one looks worn, or replace the sheet. Each trial takes a few micrometres off the pin, so one pin serves hundreds of trials.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Slurry, film, water and wear are not simulated (real trials: setup 9): the slurry spot is a painted mark and the rinse is the face's depth under a fixed water line (non-colliding water). The load cell is a stiff 10,000 N/m spring under the plate (0.5 mm at 5 N); its deflection gives the force. The tip collides as 15 mm and 9 mm square prisms (drawn round); the clamp's jaws slide on 1,500 N/m springs. Friction, the 25 g mass and the 10 mm stem are estimates to measure.
